title: Christmas tree in a car: how to fit it, tie it down and get it home
summary: A tree can ride inside if the hatch closes, or on a roof rack secured at three points. Lugg can bring home the trees that fit neither.
body_markdown:
A Christmas tree can ride inside a car when the netted tree is shorter than the usable cargo floor and the hatch closes completely. Put it on the roof only when the car has a roof rack with fixed tie-down points. According to a[2019 AAA survey](https://mwg.aaa.com/via/how/secure-christmas-tree-to-car) , 44% of Americans planned to bring a real tree home using an unsafe method, and 16% had already had a tree fall off or out of a vehicle. Lugg is an on-demand moving and delivery platform that can get a Christmas tree home from the lot when it won't fit safely inside your car or on its roof rack.


Transport option It works when The non-negotiable


Inside the car The netted tree fits with the hatch closed Keep every mirror and sight line clear


On a roof rack The rack is installed and rated for the load Stump forward, secured at the bottom, middle and top


In a pickup truck bed The bed has fixed tie-down points Stump toward the cab and no movement in any direction


No rack or a tree that is too large Don't improvise on a bare roof Use a larger vehicle or arrange delivery


## Will a Christmas tree fit in my car?


A Christmas tree fits inside your car only if its netted length is shorter than the usable cargo path and the hatch can close. Fold the rear seats, then measure from the inside of the closed hatch to the nearest point behind the front seats. Measure the narrowest part of the hatch opening too. The tree has to clear both numbers.


Measure before you leave for the lot.[AAA recommends](https://mwg.aaa.com/via/how/secure-christmas-tree-to-car) choosing the right vehicle in advance, then having the tree wrapped in netting before it is loaded. Netting compresses the branches, but it doesn't make the trunk shorter.


Don't count on cutting the tree down to solve a bad fit. A fresh slice from the bottom helps the tree take up water, but removing enough trunk to change the transport plan also changes how it sits in the stand. Buy to the measurement you took at home.


The final test is the closed car. The tree can't press against the windshield, interfere with the driver or block the mirrors. If the hatch has to stay open, choose a smaller tree or arrange[Christmas tree delivery](https://lugg.com/christmas-tree-delivery) in a vehicle that can carry it flat. An open hatch can let exhaust into the cabin and may leave lights, the license plate or the load itself improperly exposed.


## How do you put a Christmas tree inside a car?


### 1: Clear and measure the cargo path


Fold the seats you plan to use and remove anything that narrows the floor. Measure the usable length and the hatch opening before you buy the tree. Leave enough room for the hatch to close and latch.


### 2: Line the cargo area


Cover the folded seats and floor with an old sheet, tarp or moving blanket. Fresh trees shed needles and sap, and the protection makes the tree easier to slide back out at home.


### 3: Have the tree netted


Ask the lot to run the tree through its baler. A netted tree is narrower, easier to grip and less likely to snag a seat belt or interior trim. If the lot offers a fresh cut on the stump, take it so the tree can go straight into water at home.


### 4: Load it stump first


Slide the trunk end toward the front of the car. The branches fold back in their natural direction as the tree moves in, while the tip remains near the hatch where it is easiest to pull out.


### 5: Close the hatch and check every sight line


Latch the hatch fully, then sit in the driver's seat and check the windshield, side mirrors and rear visibility. If the tree interferes with the driver or the hatch won't close, unload it and use a larger vehicle.


## How do you tie a Christmas tree to a roof rack?


Put a Christmas tree on the roof only when the vehicle has a properly installed roof rack. Check the rack and vehicle manuals for load limits and approved attachment points. Lay a moving blanket between the tree and roof to protect the paint, then place the netted tree on the rack with the stump facing the front of the car.


Secure the tree at three points: near the stump, through the middle and near the top. Use strong rope or nylon ratchet straps rather than the thin twine offered at many lots. Attach each line to the rack's fixed tie-down points, and loop it around the trunk just above a branch so the tree can't slide forward under braking. Don't anchor a load to door handles, windows or trim.


Finish with a tug test. Pull the tree hard from several directions; it shouldn't move forward, backward or side to side.[AAA Northern California](https://mwg.aaa.com/news/press-release/dec-9-2024) says a badly secured tree can cause up to $1,500 in damage to paint, door seals and window frames. Drive slowly and take back roads when possible because higher speeds put more force on the tree and its tie-downs.


## Can you put a Christmas tree on a car without a roof rack?


Don't put a Christmas tree on a bare car roof. AAA found that 20% of people planning to buy a real tree expected to tie it to a roof without a rack, one of the unsafe methods in its survey. Its guidance is to put the tree inside a sufficiently large SUV, van or minivan, or use a pickup truck or a larger vehicle with a roof rack.


A blanket protects paint, but it doesn't create fixed tie-down points. Straps through door openings can damage seals or frames, and the tree can still shift. Borrowing a suitable vehicle or arranging delivery is the safer choice. A rideshare XL isn't a dependable workaround either: the driver decides what can go in the vehicle, as Lugg explains in[what Uber Courier and UberXL will actually carry](https://lugg.com/blog/use-uber-to-move-furniture) .


## How do you carry a Christmas tree in a pickup truck bed?


Lay the netted tree in the bed with the stump toward the cab, then secure it to the truck's fixed tie-down points at the bottom, middle and top. AAA found that 24% of people planning to buy a real tree expected to carry it loose in a pickup bed. The bed may look contained, but air can lift an unsecured tree just as easily as it can move one on a roof.


Run each strap around the trunk above a branch, tighten it so the tree can't slide or lift, then perform the same tug test used for a roof load. If the tree extends beyond the bed, check your state's overhang, marker and night-lighting rules before leaving the lot. If it can't be secured without excessive overhang, use a longer enclosed vehicle.


## What vehicle do you need for a 9- or 10-foot Christmas tree?


A 9- or 10-foot tree needs a cargo area long enough for it to lie flat. For Lugg bookings, the XL van is 10 feet long, the Box truck is 12 feet, and Box+ trucks run from 18 to 24 feet. Choose based on the tree's netted length; the Luggers who accept your request carry it inside to the room where it will stand. Lugg's[moving truck size guide](https://lugg.com/blog/how-big-of-a-moving-truck-do-i-need) compares the options.


Picking up a stand or decorations along the way? The same booking can include up to five stops.


## How do you get a Christmas tree home when it won't fit?


Measure your car before you shop, have the tree netted, and use only a closed cargo area or fixed tie-down points. If neither is available,[Christmas tree delivery](https://lugg.com/christmas-tree-delivery) through Lugg lets you book Luggers with the right vehicle to bring it from the lot to your home, with arrival in as little as an hour or a one-hour window you choose. Enter the addresses, choose the vehicle and review the upfront estimate before booking.
